rationale: EQT is the largest US natural gas producer — a genuinely high-quality E&P with scale advantages, integrated midstream via the 2024 Equitrans acquisition, and exceptional FCF generation ($2.84B TTM, 7.7% yield). However, the P/E-based DCF paints a consistent SELL picture: the through-cycle base case (10% revenue CAGR, 20% net margin at energy best-in-class, 12x P/E) produces $39/share — 34% below current price. The stock is priced as if elevated gas prices (~$3.50/MCF) represent the new permanent normal, not a mid-cycle mean. Weighted fair value $48.37 (-17.5%). SELL — but FCF yield (7.7%) signals genuine value if gas price thesis materializes.

bear.rationale: Natural gas prices revert to 2024 trough levels (~$1.75-2.00/MCF Henry Hub) as mild winters, LNG export delays, and efficiency improvements in gas turbines create supply glut. Revenue grows modestly (3% CAGR) via production volume growth but price headwinds offset. Net margin collapses to 8% — above FY3 actual 4.42% floor only because Equitrans integration now captures midstream margin regardless of wellhead price. ExitPE 8x = energy sector conservative floor (benchmark row). No buybacks — cash conserved through downcycle. QM 0.90: moats intact but not premium-worthy in commodity trough. This scenario mirrors 2023-2024 gas collapse; probability non-trivial given AI efficiency improvements reducing per-token compute requirements.

base.rationale: Through-cycle normalized scenario: Henry Hub ~$3.00-3.50/MCF (consistent with current). Revenue grows 10% CAGR via organic production volume growth (~5-7%/yr drilling program) + Equitrans synergy capture. Net margin 20% = energy sector best-in-class ceiling per valuation benchmarks — justified by EQT's integrated midstream position providing above-peer margin capture. The 4-year mean is 19.41%; base uses 20% as the ceiling, acknowledging that Equitrans integration structurally improves margins vs. pure E&P peers. ExitPE 12x = energy sector median (benchmark row). Two moats warrant QM 1.10: (1) lowest-cost Marcellus/Utica production structure in Appalachian basin (~$2.00/MCF break-even vs industry ~$2.50+); (2) fully integrated midstream (Equitrans pipes/compressors) — structural cost advantage that strengthens through cycles. Modest buybacks -2%/yr from strong FCF.

bull.rationale: Catalyst: AI datacenter power demand + accelerating LNG exports to Europe/Asia drive structural increase in US natural gas demand, pushing Henry Hub above $4.50-5.00/MCF on a sustained basis. EQT's low-cost Appalachian assets generate exceptional margins (30%) — approaching FY2 2023 peak of 34.23% but without the Ukraine war distortion. Revenue grows 18% CAGR via production volume acceleration + higher realized prices. ExitPE 16x = energy sector growth ceiling (benchmark row) — warranted if structural demand shift is proven. QM 1.10 unchanged — E&P companies are price-takers; even with two structural moats, 'exceptional durable pricing power across cycles' cannot be claimed for a commodity producer. Accelerated buybacks -3%/yr with $3B+ FCF. This scenario requires gas prices to remain structurally elevated — a non-trivial condition.

aiThesis.rationale:
## EQT Corporation (EQT) — Investment Thesis

**Verdict: SELL — Fair Value $48.37/share (−17.5% downside)**

*Note: FCF yield (7.7%) provides a contrarian positive signal not fully captured by P/E DCF framework. See FCF Yield Addendum below.*

EQT Corporation is the largest natural gas producer in the United States, with operations concentrated in the low-cost Appalachian basin (Marcellus/Utica shale). The July 2024 acquisition of Equitrans Midstream transformed EQT from a pure E&P into a vertically integrated producer — controlling the full value chain from wellhead gas production through gathering, compression, and interstate transmission. This is a genuinely high-quality industrial position with authentic structural advantages.

**The Case for EQT**: Natural gas demand is entering a structural growth period. AI datacenters require massive amounts of electricity — and natural gas-fired power generation remains the primary dispatchable electricity source for baseload power. EQT management has pointed to LNG export growth (European energy security + Asian demand) as a second structural tailwind. Combine production growth (~5-7%/yr from the Appalachian drilling program) with structural demand uplift, and the bull case (18% CAGR to $19B revenue, 30% margins) produces $116/share in present value — nearly 2x the current price. EQT also generates exceptional FCF: $2.84B TTM on a $36.7B market cap = 7.7% FCF yield. This is genuine, tangible cash that funds buybacks ($625M shares × -2%/yr = meaningful per-share accretion) and debt paydown from the Equitrans deal.

**The Case Against (Why SELL)**: The P/E-based DCF framework, applied rigorously with energy sector benchmarks, tells a different story. The through-cycle base case — 10% revenue CAGR, 20% net margin (energy best-in-class ceiling), 12x P/E (sector median) — produces $39/share, 34% below current price. This is not a modeling error; it reflects that EQT at $58.66 requires either (a) permanent above-historical gas prices or (b) above-sector-benchmark margin assumptions to generate positive returns. The prior Gemini model achieved BUY by using 25% base margin (exceeding the 20% energy best-in-class ceiling without explicit justification) and unvalidated QM 1.2 — both violations of the adversarial objectivity constraint.

**Commodity Risk is Real**: EQT's margin history provides a sharp reminder of commodity risk. In FY3 (2024), when Henry Hub averaged ~$2/MCF, EQT's net margin collapsed to 4.42% — from 34.23% just one year earlier (FY2 2023). A single year's gas price movement wiped out 30 percentage points of margin. This isn't ancient history; it was last year. The bear case (30% probability weight) of $5.54 present value is not exotic — it's what happens if gas prices return to 2024 trough levels. At $58.66 stock price, investors are paying for the world where 2024 does not repeat.

**FCF Yield Addendum**: The 7.7% FCF yield deserves independent mention. Under a Gordon Growth Model (perpetuity-based, not 5-year DCF), using $2.84B FCF, 10% discount rate, and 3% growth gives an intrinsic equity value of $2.84B × 1.03 / (0.10 - 0.03) × 625M^(-1) per share — or total value = $41.8B vs current $36.7B market cap = 14% undervaluation on FCF basis. This contrasts with the P/E DCF SELL. The divergence suggests EQT is modestly undervalued on a cash basis but overvalued on a normalized-earnings basis — typical for E&P companies where D&A significantly exceeds capex in the near term. For income-oriented investors focused on FCF yield, EQT may be modestly attractive. For growth-oriented investors using standard DCF, it's a SELL.

analyticsLog.shareCountMethod: Used API shares_diluted = 625,478,000 (matches shares_outstanding exactly — 0% discrepancy). Mktcap-implied = 625,477,983 (rounding only). Clean share count.
analyticsLog.marginAnchor: 4-year average 19.41% used as through-cycle anchor — mean-reverting rule applied. EQT is a commodity natural gas producer: margins are dictated by Henry Hub gas prices, NOT business operational improvements. Margin history shows extreme commodity-cycle volatility: FY1 14.59% (2022 Ukraine spike — hedging losses muted gains), FY2 34.23% (2023 — favorable hedge book), FY3 4.42% (2024 — severe gas price collapse), TTM 24.41% (recovery). Using TTM 24.41% as anchor (trending rule) would be INCORRECT — this is a mean-reverting commodity business. 4yr average 19.41% is the correct through-cycle anchor. Base 20% is capped at energy sector best-in-class per benchmark rule, with explicit thesis: Equitrans midstream integration provides above-peer margin capture vs. pure E&P.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: No analyst estimates (API returned {}). Revenue history shows acquisition-driven spike: FY1 $12.1B (2022 gas spike) → FY2 $5.1B → FY3 $5.2B → TTM $8.35B (recovery + Equitrans ~$1.6B added). TTM 49.9% YoY growth is NOT organic — driven by gas price recovery and Equitrans consolidation. Organic growth derived from: production volume growth (~5-7%/yr per drilling program) + Equitrans integration synergies (2-3%/yr over 5 yrs) = 8-10% base CAGR. Bear 3%: stable production, flat/declining gas prices. Bull 18%: production acceleration + gas price surge from AI/LNG structural demand.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Energy — Integrated Oil: conservative P/E 8, median P/E 12, growth P/E 16. Net margin typical 5-15%, best-in-class 20%. Note: EQT is classified as Oil & Gas E&P but post-Equitrans acquisition is functionally closer to Integrated Oil (production + gathering + transmission). Using Integrated Oil benchmark as most appropriate available row. Bull exitPE 16x = growth ceiling — justified only if structural AI/LNG demand thesis is proven at scale.
